create.title: Uniform lower-wavelet localization and exact low-two-adic survivor
create.statement_tex: Let R=X^(1/4), y=floor(sqrt X), N=floor X, W(k)=hat J(k)-hat J(k+1), and B_flat^(N)=sum_k D_N(k)W(k) be the exact Round-121 lower discrepancy. For every fixed A>=1, |W(k)| is at most a constant times (R+|k|)^(-1)(1+|k|/y)^(-A), while sum_k|W(k)|<<log X and sum_k|kW(k)|<<y. Fix 0<delta<1/8, K_delta=yX^delta, and A_0=ceil(log_2 R). The ranges |k|>K_delta and |k|<=R, the cumulative increments v_2(N+j)>=A_0, and the odd positive-character central complementary band are all O_(epsilon,delta)(RX^epsilon). If m=2^a n with n odd, a(n)=sum_(d|n)chi_4(d)=r_2(m)/4, T_z(n)=sum_(q|n,q<z)chi_4(q), and V_delta(m) equals a(n)/2 for a=0 and chi_4(n)=1, T_(n/y)(n) for a=0 and chi_4(n)=-1, a(n)-chi_4(n)T_(n/y)(n) for 1<=a<A_0, and zero for a>=A_0, then B_flat^(N)=sum_(R<|k|<=K_delta)W(k) I_k V_delta+O_(epsilon,delta)(RX^epsilon), where I_k is the exact oriented interval from N to N+k. All centering and overlap seams are included. This is a target-scale reduction, not an estimate of the displayed survivor.
create.next_action: Prove one genuinely joint signed RX^epsilon bound for the exact medium-index low-two-adic survivor. Keep all residue, valuation, full-divisor, complement, and wavelet labels together.

create.title: All-two-adic complementary-divisor self-return for the lower sharp cone
create.statement_tex: For every positive m=2^a n with n odd, the exact sharp coefficient satisfies A_y(m)=a(n)-chi_4(n)T_(n/y)(n), where a(n)=r_2(m)/4 and T_z(n)=sum_(q|n,q<z)chi_4(q). The complement is d<->n/d=m/(2^a d); using m/d for a>=1 leaves the character support. The strict lower-tail boundary accounts exactly for d=y and every square fixed point. If chi_4(n)=-1 then a(n)=0 and A_y(m)=T_(n/y)(n), so the involution returns the truncated coefficient without contraction. If chi_4(n)=1 it leaves one half of the full r_2/4 coefficient plus an exact central band; the odd near-square central band is target-safe, but low even bands are generally wide. Completing the full coefficient and subtracting its complement reconstructs the original d<=y product cone. Thus complementary divisors alone yield no power saving. This is not a signed lower bound for the complete survivor.
create.next_action: Freeze a second complement, residuewise or valuationwise norms, and full-r_2 completion followed by a circle estimate. Reopen only with a new joint signed inequality on the exact survivor.

reject.reason: The one-sided cutoff changes at scale 1/y. Uniform Fourier decay requires explicit derivative norms growing as powers of y.
For m=2^a n with a>=1 and contributing odd d, m/d is even and has zero character. The character-preserving complement is n/d=m/(2^a d).
chi_4(m)=0 for even m. The lawful sign is chi_4(n) on the odd part.
Only a=0 has threshold n/y=y+O(X^delta). For a>=1 the threshold is y/2^a+O(X^delta/2^a), so the band is generally wide.
A constant factor cannot supply the missing power, and the positive-character identity retains the full r_2/4 coefficient plus its exact central term.
The full coefficient and exact complementary tail occur together once. Separating them exposes the open circle estimate; recombining restores the original sharp cone.
A localized pre-Abel sum requires a boundary or an independently controlled Fourier tail. The accepted proof instead uses the exact localized cumulative correction and displays every overlap.
The proved projection applies to every increment N+j in the oriented cumulative interval, not merely to v_2(N+k).
The result is an algebraic no-go for this mechanism. Cancellation across k, valuations, residues, and full/complement labels remains possible in the actual signed survivor.
The medium-index low-two-adic survivor remains open. Even a future GAR theorem would control total active M1, not either direct blockwise M1 parent.
